title: Ring Dem Bells and the Palladium triumph
summary: Greer opens under a spotlight, plays tympani arpeggios and the audience cheers.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Yeah, so after he sit down, she resumed her act. Now, at about 15 minutes intermission before the second part of the show come on, us, they opened the show with us. Now, we had been back there tasting, and everybody feeling fine, fine. No pain. Like I told you, we had our own stage, own stage rolled down and rolled back, had our own lights, the pinpoint lights, so Duke say, I want the stage completely dark, one pinpoint spot on Sonny because we opened with "Ring Dem Bells" and the stage is dark, the only thing you see -- the first thing you see is me, all them drums and chimes, da, da ------ man, I was --

The curtain broke, and the spot's on me and all you can is my face and my hands, hitting anything. I don't know whether it was right or wrong. Just making some noise. Man, about the eighth bar, they stood up, standing ovation. They hadn't seen the whole band yet. Stood up, cheers.

Cheers, youhear me? No exaggeration. I'm telling you like it was. Cheers. They got through the first number, then come Bailey and Derby, the dancers, two dancers, So, man, them cats could lay some wood, they could dance. So they come out and done their act and broke it up. So they act -- and me, I had never done that before, everytime they come out, I threw

arpeggio on the tympani, pedal--on tympani you know. That's what they call milking. I scared them half to death, so when they come off and we done that, everyone -- Ivie come up, naturally we killed them, and we closed our act with "Mood Indigo". Tricky and Barney and Lawrence -- no, Tricky -- who was it -- it was Tricky and Lawrence Brown and Carney come down and played just plain sweet melody and I was singing with the band then. And I was singing a high obbligato in back of it. It was faint, haunting, you know, that's how we closed.
Boy, I'm telling you -- it's on the writeup there. Did you ever see the writeup?
No. : Go ahead, we'll look at it after you show us.

So anyway when I come off, we had in my dressing room, Derby and Bailey, a whole big quart of booze. Say, "Man, keep that in, that bow, that was a highlight for us, keep that in." I said, "Man,...". They said, "No, you got to keep that in," so I kept it in all the way. Surefire, they're still bowing.

You know, it was so unexpected to see how things come to you. I had no idea of doing that, but just out of the (Unintelligible) on my left, I got mallets clear, just experimenting and I just on the/ and did arpeggio, and did the arpeggio on the pedal, I had no idea of doing that with them, but like something you feel like you're doing, you do it, and I did and they loved it.
